chunk-001:c001.proposition: Atheism alone supplies no positive social program, while secular-humanist values held by some atheists can contribute constructively to a better world.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source independently distinguishes bare atheism from the affirmative values packaged by secular humanism, so the proposition directly states the con route without requiring an opposing move.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Intolerant exclusion and punitive political dogmatism arise from human ideologies and behavior rather than from atheism as their foundation.

orphanFallback.rationale: Even without the earlier attribution of secular intolerance, the excerpt supports the affirmative distinction that rigid exclusion is produced by dogmatic ideology rather than entailed by atheism.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Reported benefits of religiosity may derive from self-reporting pressures and supportive community rather than religious truth, and secular organizations can reproduce the community mechanism.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source supplies a standalone natural explanation for reported religious benefits and expressly identifies community-building as a mechanism available to secular organizations.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Secular humanism can sustain awe, commitments beyond oneself, social concern, and community without either supernatural belief or coercive state atheism.

orphanFallback.rationale: The excerpt affirmatively identifies awe, higher commitments, concern, and community as secular possibilities while distinguishing secular humanism from state-enforced atheism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Secular humanism can inherit valuable ideas from Christianity and other traditions while discarding supernatural claims and harmful scriptural baggage because humans transmit and revise moral ideas.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source independently advocates taking good ideas wherever found and rejecting the rest, grounding moral inheritance and revision in human transmission rather than divine authorship.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Appealing to God does not resolve why anyone should care about morality, whereas demonstrable human concern and well-being provide a more direct basis without unsupported theological assumptions.

orphanFallback.rationale: The excerpt independently contrasts observable human interests with the unanswered demand to obey God, providing a constructive secular basis even absent the preceding divine-foundation claim.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Secular humanism offers no guarantee of a better world but improves comparatively by centering human interests, retaining useful inherited ideas, and rejecting harmful doctrines such as biblical slavery.

orphanFallback.rationale: The excerpt directly answers the motion by presenting human welfare, selective inheritance, and rejection of harmful biblical commitments as affirmative comparative features of secular humanism.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: A workable moral system can begin from shared concern for human beings and deliberate from that agreement, while an undemonstrated divine premise prevents common inquiry from getting started.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source affirmatively proposes agreement that humans matter as the operational starting point for moral reasoning and explains why an unestablished God premise cannot serve that shared function.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Human lives can have immense value to human beings without possessing an intrinsic value conferred by the universe or a divine source.

orphanFallback.rationale: The excerpt directly affirms substantial human valuation while denying cosmic intrinsic value, making the same proposition a standalone secular account of dignity and concern.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Consequences for shared well-being make oppressive and exclusionary systems morally assessable even though secular judgments remain corrigible and may later prove mistaken.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source independently uses wider social consequences to assess oppressive practices and openly preserves revisability, supplying a constructive account of an expandable moral circle.
